name: South Australian Pidgin English
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct pidgin; Glottolog refs are historical/classificatory, no phonological description located

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'South Australian Pidgin English' (read 2026-09-17); sourced entirely from Foster, Monaghan & Mühlhäusler 2003.
sources.note: Nothing; repeats the PL-538 segmental substitutions and cluster reduction only.

sources.citation: Foster, Robert, Paul Monaghan & Peter Mühlhäusler. 2003. Early forms of Aboriginal English in South Australia, 1840s-1920s. (Pacific Linguistics 538.) Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. xxxii+102 pp.http://hdl.handle.net/1885/146166(CC BY 4.0).
sources.note: Nothing. The Introduction's 'Phonology' section (p. xvi, p.16) covers only segmental substitutions in the written record (f>p 'pish', v>b 'bery', th>t/d 'tink', sh>ch 'choogah') and consonant-cluster reduction ('ky', 'gubnor'); a full-text search of the volume for stress/accent/intonation/prosody/syllable returns no relevant hits.

sources.citation: Dineen, Anne & Peter Mühlhäusler. 1996. Nineteenth century language contact in South Australia. In Wurm, Mühlhäusler & Tryon (eds), Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas, vol. II.1, 83-100. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
